newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima says may hold briefing on restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima says may hold briefing on restructuring.

text.p: Japanese general contractor Tobishima Corp said it may hold a news conference at around 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT) on Friday about its new restructuring programme.
A Tobishima spokesman said the company was likely to explain its new restructuring plan, but declined to give any further details.

The spokesman also declined to confirm a newspaper report on Friday which said Fuji Bank Ltd and Tobishima, which is burdened with property-related debts, have agreed on a restructuring plan for Tobishima.

Japanese economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that the new plan agreed with Fuji proposes that creditor financial institutions should not hold Tobishima responsible for bad debts worth about 650 billion yen which it transferred to one of its units under a previous restructuring programme.
Under the 1992 restructuring plan, Tobishima had guaranteed the debts, the newspaper said.

Under the new restructuring programme, Tobishima will also ask creditor institutions to further cut interest rates on its debts, the newspaper said. There are more than 30 creditor institutions including Fuji, the paper said.
Earlier, a Fuji Bank spokesman said Tobishima was forming a new restructuring plan, but gave no further details.
Tobishima Corp shares were trading at 448 yen at 0522 GMT on Friday against their Thursday close at 416 yen.
